It was timed to be near the German retreat, but before the Soviets came (as it was a goal of the Polish Underground State to liberate Poland's capital and assert Polish sovereignty before the Soviet-backed Polish Committee of National Liberation, an unpopular opposition to the Polish Government in exile (in London) could take control). When the Soviets approached the eastern suburbs of the city, the Red Army halted temporarily, enabling Germans to regroup and defeat the Polish resistance, and destroy about 85% of the city.

The Uprising was fought for 63 days with little outside support, and is today the single largest military effort taken by any European resistance movement during WW2.
